correctness.rationale: The exact geometric sample is two independent arclength-distributed boundary endpoints on a fixed strictly convex positively curved C^3 oval, not a random invariant line. Strict convexity localizes small midpoint depth to short endpoint gap h; unit-speed Frenet expansion gives D(s,h)=kappa(s)h^2/8+o(h^2) uniformly, and compact positive curvature makes |h|=O(sqrt(epsilon)). The (s,h) to (s,z) Jacobian is sqrt(8epsilon/kappa(s)) with z=h sqrt(kappa(s))/sqrt(8epsilon). Dominated convergence with common compact z-support yields L1 joint-density convergence to sqrt(8) f(s)^2/kappa(s)^1/2 times 1_{|z|<1}; normalization gives 4sqrt2*J(f) probability coefficient and the exact stated total-variation conditional location/uniform signed-mark law. Depth mark converges only weakly via z^2, producing Beta(1/2,1). Cauchy–Schwarz gives J>=1/H with equality f∝sqrt(kappa); H^2<=2pi L implies global 4/sqrt(pi L) unique circle/uniform equality. Ellipse curvature kappa=ab/q^3 implies uniform-density J diverges as b^-1/2 at fixed perimeter, and continuous axis ratio covers every coefficient above circular minimum. Independent exact circle calculation matched coefficient 2sqrt2/(pi sqrt(R)); the source ellipse sampler is diagnostic, not a proof.

value.rationale: PASS: sharp local curvature-dependent rare-event asymptotic for a natural independent-boundary chord sampling model, including a strong total-variation marked law and unique optimal density, yields exact quantitative geometric sampling design across all smooth positively curved ovals. The fixed-perimeter disk optimizer and unbounded anisotropy connect local curvature with global extremal geometry; it is not merely the known circle chord distribution or a restatement of a different Beer-index shell model.

limitations: No uniformity over degenerating curves, cornered/nonconvex bodies, higher dimensions or epsilon-dependent boundary laws.
Known disk special case and shared curvature integral are credited; only the full smooth-oval marked law and optimization survive as novel.
